brief.t: Founded in Mangalore in July 1906 by Ammembal Subba Rao Pai; head office now in Bengaluru.
A public sector bank: the Government of India owns 62.93% of its shares (Sep 2026). Syndicate Bank merged into it on 1 April 2020.
Brajesh Kumar Singh, earlier Executive Director of Indian Bank, became MD & CEO on 1 June 2026, after K. Satyanarayana Raju retired in Dec 2025.
FY 2025-26 standalone net profit rose 12.7% to ₹19,187 crore; Gross NPA fell to 1.84% from 2.94%.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit rose 8.4% to ₹5,175 crore; Gross NPA improved further to 1.33%.

timeline.t: Founded in Mangalore by Ammembal Subba Rao Pai.
Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank.
Subsidiaries Canara Robeco AMC and Canara HSBC Life listed on the stock exchanges through IPOs.
Opened its 10,000th branch, at Budigere Cross, Bengaluru, on its 120th Founders' Day.
Brajesh Kumar Singh took charge as MD & CEO.

model.how: Canara Bank earns mainly from the gap between interest on loans and interest paid on deposits, plus fees. It lends heavily to retail, farm and MSME borrowers (its 'RAM' book), and earns from subsidiaries in insurance, mutual funds and housing finance.
flow: Bank lends to people, farmers, MSMEs and companies

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Government of India (as main owner)
points: The Government appoints the MD & CEO of public sector banks; Canara Bank had an interim chief for about five months in 2026.
Public sector banks merged into fewer, bigger banks in 2019–2020; Canara Bank absorbed Syndicate Bank.
Big theme for interviews: banks listing their insurance and mutual fund arms to unlock value, as Canara did in 2025.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Amalgamation: Two or more companies combining into one. Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank in 2020.
glossary.IBPS: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, which runs common recruitment exams for public sector banks.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public. Canara Bank sold part of its stake in two subsidiaries through IPOs in 2025.
glossary.RAM credit: Retail, Agriculture and MSME loans: the small-borrower part of a bank's loan book.

Personality, banking knowledge and HR questions

Finance.q: How did Canara Bank cut Gross NPA from 2.94% to 1.33% in about 18 months?
Finance.a: Better recoveries, write-offs of old bad loans, fewer new defaults and fast loan growth, which also spreads bad loans over a bigger book.

Finance.q: Why did Canara Bank sell stakes in its AMC and life insurance arms?
Finance.a: To unlock value and raise money without issuing new bank shares, while still keeping control as promoter.

Marketing.q: Canara Bank removed minimum-balance charges on all savings accounts in 2025. How would you promote that?
Marketing.a: Simple 'no minimum balance' messaging for students, first-time earners and rural customers, through branches, the app and local-language campaigns.

Marketing.q: How would you sell Canara HSBC Life policies through bank branches?
Marketing.a: Train staff to match plans to customer needs, target home-loan and salary customers, and explain benefits honestly.

HR.q: How would you manage 81,000+ employees through a change in MD & CEO?
HR.a: Clear communication from the new leader, stable priorities, recognition and regular town halls across zones.

Sales.q: Sell a Canara Bank savings account to a college student.
Sales.a: Ask about needs, then link zero minimum balance, UPI and the app, and a trusted 120-year-old bank. Close with a next step.

Operations.q: RBI fined Canara Bank for KYC lapses. How would you fix KYC operations?
Operations.a: Automated uploads to the central KYC registry, daily exception reports, clear owner per branch and regular audits.

Other.q: What do you know about Canara Bank?
Other.a: A public sector bank founded in 1906 in Mangalore, HQ Bengaluru, led by MD & CEO Brajesh Kumar Singh, with ₹19,187 cr FY26 profit and over 10,000 branches.

gd.t: Should public sector banks list their subsidiaries?
gd.for: Listing unlocks value and brings market discipline, as with Canara Robeco and Canara HSBC Life.
gd.against: Selling stakes reduces the bank's share of future profits.

gd.for: It helps poorer customers and builds trust, as Canara Bank did in 2025.
gd.against: Banks lose fee income and may cut other services.
